models._description: Sparse fields Test (TransientModel — demo/test fixture only)
Adds _valid_field_parameter to accept 'sparse' as a recognized field parameter
Adds 'serialized' ttype and serialization_field_id linkage; guards rename/reparent of sparse fields

behavioral_notes.element: fields.py — monkey_patch / fields.Field._get_attrs: sparse field wiring at class-definition time
behavioral_notes.observation: The module monkey-patches fields.Field using a decorator-based monkey_patch(cls) helper that saves the original method as func.super. _get_attrs is patched so that if attrs.get('sparse') is truthy, the field is made non-stored (store=False), non-copied by default (copy=False unless explicitly set), compute is wired to self._compute_sparse, and — if not readonly — inverse is wired to self._inverse_sparse. The sparse parameter is just a string naming the Serialized host field. The net effect: any field declared with sparse='<serialized_field_name>' becomes a computed+inverse field with no DB column of its own, backed entirely by a JSON TEXT column.

_compute_sparse iterates records, reads record[self.sparse] (the Serialized JSON dict), and assigns values.get(self.name) to record[self.name]; for relational fields it additionally calls .exists() to discard stale ids (avoids broken Many2one references after record deletion). _inverse_sparse calls self.convert_to_read(record[self.name], record, use_display_name=False) to obtain a serialisable value; if truthy and different from the stored value it updates the dict and writes back record[self.sparse] = values; if falsy it pops the key entirely — so absent/null sparse values are never stored in the JSON, keeping the dict compact. Both methods work entirely through the ORM cache layer with no direct SQL.

behavioral_notes.element: fields.py — class Serialized(fields.Field): the column-level storage type
behavioral_notes.observation: Serialized is a concrete fields.Field subclass with type='serialized' and column_type=('text','text') — maps to a PostgreSQL TEXT column. prefetch=False prevents batch-loading in normal queries (avoids pulling large JSON blobs when other fields are prefetched). convert_to_cache stores the value as json.dumps(value, default=json_default) if isinstance(value, dict), else None — cache format is a JSON string or None. convert_to_record calls json.loads(value or '{}') — always returns a dict to callers. convert_to_column_insert delegates to convert_to_cache ensuring INSERTs and UPDATEs see the same serialised form. fields.Serialized = Serialized registers the type on the fields namespace so other modules can use fields.Serialized().

behavioral_notes.element: models.py — ir.model.fields._reflect_fields: ORM registry -> ir_model_fields synchronisation for serialization_field_id
behavioral_notes.observation: _reflect_fields overrides the base method, calls super() first (structural reflection finishes), then runs a raw SQL SELECT on ir_model_fields to read (model, name, id, serialization_field_id) for all affected model names. For each model's _fields entries where field.sparse is set, it resolves the target serialisation field's id from the same result set; misses raise UserError('Serialization field not found'). Changed mappings are batched by target value and emitted as UPDATE ir_model_fields SET serialization_field_id=%s WHERE id IN %s (one statement per distinct value to minimise round-trips). pool.post_init(records.modified, ['serialization_field_id']) marks the ORM cache dirty post-install.

behavioral_notes.element: models.py — ir.model.fields.write + _instanciate_attrs: immutability guards and dynamic field reconstruction
behavioral_notes.observation: write() enforces two immutability rules: (1) changing serialization_field_id on a field that already has one raises UserError('Changing the storing system for field … is not allowed') — storage binding is fixed after creation; (2) renaming a sparse field (field.serialization_field_id set and new name != old name) raises UserError('Renaming sparse field … is not allowed'). _instanciate_attrs reads field_data['serialization_field_id'], browses the ir.model.fields record to obtain its name, and sets attrs['sparse'] = serialization_record.name — so sparse fields dynamically created via ir.model.fields (Studio/API) are correctly reconstructed with the sparse parameter at instantiation time without requiring a Python module reload.

it_architecture.application: base_sparse_field (ORM framework extension: adds a 'Serialized' field type and 'sparse' parameter to pack multiple logical fields into a single JSON TEXT column, circumventing PostgreSQL's 1600-column-per-table limit)
data_objects: fields.Serialized (new field class: type='serialized', column_type text/text, prefetch=False)
sparse_fields.test (TransientModel: unit-test/demo fixture with 1 Serialized + 6 sparse fields)
logical_data_erm: sparse_field.serialization_field_id -> ir.model.fields (the Serialized host; immutable after create)
sparse_field value stored inside Serialized TEXT/JSON dict — no own DB column
sparse_fields.test.data (Serialized) aggregates: boolean, integer, float, char, selection, partner
information_flows: import-time: models/fields.py monkey-patches fields.Field at Python module import (before ORM registry build)
field-compute path: read sparse_field -> _compute_sparse -> record[self.sparse] dict -> .get(self.name) -> typed value
field-inverse path: write sparse_field -> _inverse_sparse -> convert_to_read -> JSON dict update/pop -> record[self.sparse] = values
reflection path: module install -> ir.model.fields._reflect_fields -> raw SQL read ir_model_fields -> UPDATE serialization_field_id -> pool.post_init modified
dynamic-field path: ir.model.fields._instanciate_attrs -> browse serialization_field_id -> attrs['sparse'] = name

capabilities: Declare N logical fields (Boolean, Integer, Float, Char, Selection, Many2one, …) backed by a single JSON TEXT column, avoiding PostgreSQL column-count exhaustion
Automatic compute/inverse wiring for all sparse fields — consuming modules write no custom compute methods
Compact JSON storage: falsy/null sparse values are omitted from the dict, keeping the column lean
Graceful handling of deleted relational targets via .exists() guard in _compute_sparse
ORM reflection of sparse field metadata into ir.model.fields (serialization_field_id linkage discoverable in Settings > Technical > Fields)
Dynamic reconstruction of sparse fields created via ir.model.fields API/Studio (_instanciate_attrs)
value_streams: Module-definition stream: developer declares fields.Serialized() + fields.X(sparse='data') -> _get_attrs wires compute/inverse at class load -> no extra DB columns created
Data-read stream: UI/ORM read sparse_field -> _compute_sparse -> parse JSON TEXT -> return typed Python value
Data-write stream: UI/ORM write sparse_field -> _inverse_sparse -> serialise value -> update JSON TEXT column (or pop key if falsy)
Reflection stream: module install -> _reflect_fields -> serialization_field_id links written in ir_model_fields -> sparse field relationships visible in Settings
information_concepts: sparse parameter (str attr on fields.Field: name of the Serialized host)
serialization_field_id (ir.model.fields Many2one: the reflection of the sparse->Serialized relationship)
policies: Sparse field is always non-stored (store=False) — JSON column is sole persistence
Sparse field is non-copied by default (copy=False) unless the declaring code overrides it
serialization_field_id is immutable after creation (write() guard: UserError on change)
Sparse field names cannot be renamed after creation (write() guard: UserError on rename)
Falsy values are removed from the JSON dict (not stored as null) — the JSON remains sparse
stakeholders: Odoo module developers needing many optional fields on a model near PostgreSQL's 1600-column ceiling
Studio/low-code users adding ad-hoc optional fields without requiring DBA involvement
DBA/ops team (benefit: fewer ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN statements, narrower table width)
metrics: Number of sparse fields per model (density indicator for the JSON column)
Serialized TEXT column size growth (observable via pg_column_size on the host column)

classification.rationale: base_sparse_field is pure ORM framework infrastructure: a developer-facing extension that introduces a new field type (Serialized) and a sparse parameter to manage database schema width. It owns no business model (sparse_fields.test is a transient test fixture), has 0 routes, 0 business views, application=False, category=Hidden. Its value is entirely as shared IT plumbing allowing other modules to stay within PostgreSQL's 1600-column limit. Porter support activity; Stabell & Fjeldstad 'support' (infrastructure capability enabling all other activities). APQC 8.0 'Manage Information Technology' is the correct fit: this is database schema engineering — a technology management concern, not a business capability. 13.0 was considered and rejected: this is DB engine augmentation, not master-data management.

standard_capabilities: Declare fields.Serialized() as a JSON TEXT host column on any model
Declare any field type with sparse='<host_field>' to store its value in that JSON with zero extra SQL columns
Automatic compute/inverse wiring — no custom @api.depends or write() required on consuming models
Relational sparse fields (Many2one) work correctly: .exists() guards stale ids on read
ir.model.fields reflection: sparse fields display serialization_field_id in Settings > Technical > Fields
Protection against renaming or reparenting sparse fields after initial creation
typical_fits: Adding many optional/rarely-used configurable attributes to a model already near PostgreSQL's 1600-column ceiling
Storing product-variant or configuration-specific attributes in a single column without schema migrations
Low-code/Studio scenarios adding ad-hoc optional fields without DBA involvement
common_gaps: Sparse fields cannot be searched via ORM domain syntax — they are computed non-stored fields; SQL filtering requires custom query or a stored computed field
No group-by or aggregate support on individual sparse field values — SQL aggregation needs the host JSON column
Renaming a sparse field after creation requires a data migration (name immutability guard blocks the normal path)
Converting an existing stored field to sparse after a table already has data is not supported
No automatic indexing of individual sparse keys (no GIN/btree on JSON keys by default)
